text:
leah: noticed a weird thing in Insights usage heatmap. when i change the time window fast (last 1h -> 7d -> 1h) the "top-runs" side panel sometimes shows rows from the previously selected org for ~4s. saw it on prod at 14:20 UTC.

tonio: ugh. can you share repro steps?

leah: simple:
1) org-A user, open Insights -> Usage Heatmap
2) open side panel Top Runs (calls /internal/top-runs)
3) quick switch time window 1h -> 7d -> 1h
4) panel briefly lists run ids belonging to org-B (weird) then refreshes to correct org-A rows

patrick: i can repro on staging using fastclick stress test. looks like the panel's cache key isn't including the org in some code path. grabbing network logs.

leah: network capture:
GET /internal/top-runs?window=1h 200 OK
Response JSON meta: {"org":"org-B","count":10} <-- while the page context shows org-A
Headers sent: x-org-id: org-A, cookie: s=...

tonio: hmm headers say org-A but payload meta.org org-B. that suggests backend returned stale data or a proxy returned cached response for a different org. any edge caches?

patrick: we have edge-cache + internal reverse proxy that memoizes by request path only. most internal calls rely on x-org-id for sharding but cache key was misconfigured to not include x-org-id for /internal/top-runs. this was an optimization gone wrong (cache key normalization).

leah: so a user from org-A could see org-B's top runs if the path + query matched and the edge cache returned a cached body. that's bad. P0? P1?

tonio: surface exposure is read-only and transient, but it's cross-tenant leakage of metadata. i'd call it P1 and remediate immediately.

patrick: quick mitigation: update proxy cache config to include header x-org-id in cache key for any /internal/* endpoints. i'll push a config change to canary and purge suspicious keys.

patrick: also found a second layer: client-side ReplayCache wrapper in console that caches responses keyed by URL only (no header). that means even after proxy fix, client could reuse wrong cached entry when user flips time windows rapidly.

leah: can you paste the culprit snippet?

patrick: snippet below:
```
// console/replayCache.js
const cache = new Map()
export async function cachedFetch(url) {
  if (cache.has(url)) return cache.get(url)
  const res = await fetch(url)
  cache.set(url, res.clone())
  return res
}
```

patrick: i searched, a lot of panels use cachedFetch for perf. cache key needs to include x-org-id or context param.

tonio: short-term: change cachedFetch to accept an optional cacheKey param and default to `${url}|${ctx.org}` where ctx.org is passed from caller. also add a telemetry counter `console.cache.cross_tenant_leak` when res.meta.org !== ctx.org.

leah: logging/telemetry: we should emit an audit log when a response contains a mismatched org in meta. add sampling to avoid huge noise.

infra-bot: alert: config change staged to canary at 1750003370. cache purge in progress for /internal/top-runs keys.

patrick: i've raised PR #8402 with two fixes: (1) proxy cache key includes x-org-id for internal endpoints (2) cachedFetch updated and callers patched. added unit tests and an e2e that does rapid window flips under concurrent users.

tonio: rollout plan: land to canary -> monitor `console.cache.cross_tenant_leak` and `audit.log.mismatched_orgs` for 2h -> 10% prod -> 50% -> 100%. kill-switch: revert proxy config and clear client caches via version bump.

leah: excellent. i've filed a customer-notify draft in #support-template in case we want to proactively message any impacted accounts. probably safe to hold unless we see evidence of targeted exposure.

patrick: canary deployed at 1750003385 (service/console-api v2.14.4-canary). verified no repro under stress test.

infra-bot: prod rollout scheduled: next deploy window 16:00 UTC if canary looks good.

leah: thanks everyone. assigning follow-ups: patrick->postmortem + PR merge, tonio->telemetry + alert rule, me->support draft. closing thread unless anything new shows up. :eyes:
